tests.name: Sun and Earth positions vs NASA JPL Horizons
tests.what: Azimuth and elevation of the Sun and Earth from 6 sites, every 7h from 2026-01-01 00:00 to 2026-06-01 00:00 UTC (6216 comparisons). Ours: SPICE (DE440, MOON_ME, CN+S) + pipeline/geometry.py. Horizons: coord@301, QUANTITIES 4, airless.
tests.explanation: Largest angle on the sky between our direction and Horizons'. Small remaining differences come from light-time measured from the Moon's centre (ours) vs from the site (Horizons) and from Horizons' gravitational light bending.

tests.name: Time trap: UTC fed in as TDB
tests.what: V1 for the equator Sun again, but every time is shifted by -69.184 s, the mistake of treating clock time (UTC) as TDB.
tests.tolerance: must exceed the V1 target of 0.002 deg (expected about 0.0098 deg)
tests.explanation: The Sun crosses the lunar sky at about 0.0085 deg per minute, so a 69.2 s clock mistake moves it about 0.0098 deg. This test failing proves V1 is sensitive enough to catch time-scale bugs.

tests.name: Sun height at the exact pole (smooth Moon)
tests.what: Sun height every 6 h, 2023-2032, a hair from 90 S, no terrain, no mast.
tests.explanation: At the pole the Sun never rises more than the tilt of the Moon's equator allows. The plan expected 1.54 deg (the mean tilt, 1.543 deg); the true maximum is larger because of physical libration and the Moon's orbital tilt. The day-one kernel check found 1.587 deg in both MOON_ME and IAU_MOON (docs/kernel_checks.txt), so the expected value was corrected to 1.59 deg. Against the original 1.54 deg this test would fail.

tests.name: Equator (0, 0), smooth Moon
tests.what: Every 10 minutes, 2023-2032, 2 m mast, any part of the Sun counts as up.
tests.tolerance: Sun up 50 +/- 0.5 %; mean day 14.77 +/- 0.4 d; Earth always up, at least ~79 deg high
tests.explanation: Mean day 14.85 d over 122 complete lunar days (slightly over 14.77 d because the Sun's edge and the mast add minutes at each end). Earth stays at least 79.56 deg high. Eclipses (72.8 h in the decade) darken the Sun but are not counted as sunsets.

tests.name: Far side (Chang'e-4): Earth never visible
tests.what: Earth's height every hour, 2023-2032, at 45.4446 S, 177.5991 E (Liu et al. 2019), smooth Moon.
tests.tolerance: no part of Earth ever above the horizon; centre about -37 to -53 deg
tests.explanation: Earth's centre stays between -51.6 and -37.1 deg (mean -44.5 deg): libration rocks it up and down but never brings it close to the horizon. Direct-to-Earth contact is impossible there, which is why Chang'e-4 needed the Queqiao relay satellite.

tests.name: Total lunar eclipse of 2025-03-14 seen from the Moon
tests.what: Fraction of the Sun not covered by Earth, every minute 06:26-07:31 UTC, at (0, 0).
tests.explanation: During totality the whole Moon is in Earth's shadow, so Earth hides the Sun completely. At this single point the Sun is covered from 2025-03-14T05:45:00 to 2025-03-14T08:10:00 UTC, longer than totality, which needs the whole Moon inside the shadow. Earth is drawn as a solid disc (no atmosphere).

tests.name: Connecting Ridge average sunlight vs published research
tests.what: Average visible part of the Sun's disc, every hour 2023-2032, at 89.4395 S, 222.8066 E, 2 m mast, using M3's LOLA horizon mask.
tests.tolerance: within 5 points of about 88% (Glaser et al. 2018)
tests.explanation: Ours 87.9% vs about 88% published. Longest continuous darkness 4.71 d vs 4.58 d in Glaser et al. 2014, who used a different period. Differences come from the terrain model and the years averaged.
